title: Enterprise cost & commitment routing decision canvas for billing/pricing requests
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Problem: We receive a growing number of non-bug customer requests touching pricing, commitments, invoicing, and marketplace listing economics. Current routing is inconsistent: some requests go to Solutions Eng, some to Sales Ops, some to Finance, and PMs frequently get pulled into tactical estimations without clear decision criteria. This creates slow SLAs, inconsistent customer-facing answers, and ad-hoc tradeoffs that impact revenue recognition and risk.

Objective: Deliver an operational Decision Canvas + Intake Matrix that standardizes how PM and cross-functional teams triage pricing/commitment/billing requests from customers, partners, and internal stakeholders. The canvas should: 1) define clear ownership for each request class; 2) provide deterministic prioritization inputs (revenue impact, urgency, compliance risk, implementation effort, repeatability); 3) prescribe template responses and SLA targets; 4) surface when an ask must become a product requirement vs a sales/finance exception; 5) include example scenarios and guardrails for marketplace and invoicing cases.

Why it matters: Faster, consistent replies reduce deal friction, reduce downstream rework, and improve telemetry for product decisions (we need to quantify revenue ops lift). This also reduces legal/compliance exposure for non-standard contract terms and clarifies when engineering changes (billing integrations, metering) are required.

Deliverables: 1) Decision Canvas document (Confluence) with matrix and flowchart; 2) Triage checklist & intake form (Google Form / internal Zendesk template); 3) Routing rules config for the intake system (CSV) and playbook with response templates; 4) Small pilot with Sales Ops + 3 customer reps for 2 weeks; 5) Metrics dashboard (Looker) tracking SLA, route accuracy, and revenue-at-risk for common request types.

Scope & out-of-scope: In scope: non-bug enterprise requests about pricing tiers, committed usage discounts, invoicing cadence, cost-allocation tags, marketplace listing fees, and contract-level billing exceptions. Out-of-scope: tax/legal contract redlines, one-off enterprise legal negotiations that require bespoke counsel, and purely technical runtime optimization requests (these belong to Eng/infra).

Stakeholders: PM (owner: Maya), Sales Ops (primary partner), Finance (billing + revenue ops), Legal (for guardrails), Solutions Eng / Customer Success (triage + templates), Platform Engineering (if implementation required).
acceptance_criteria: Canvas published in Confluence with decision matrix and flowchart
Intake form built and accessible to Sales/CS with auto-routing rules documented
Pilot executed with Sales Ops and 3 AE/CS reps for at least 10 requests each
Looker dashboard created showing SLA, routing accuracy, and revenue exposure for pilot period
Playbook approved by Finance and Legal (email confirmation or Confluence sign-off)
triage_matrix: High level matrix columns: Request Type | Revenue Impact (high/med/low) | Compliance Risk (high/med/low) | Implementation Effort (S/M/L) | Repeatability (one-off / recurring) | Owner (Sales Ops / Finance / PM / Eng) | Routing Action (Auto-approve template / Requires Finance approval / Convert to product requirement ticket). Rules: - Revenue Impact >= high & Implementation Effort > S -> escalate to PM + Eng evaluation. - Compliance Risk high -> route to Legal + Finance immediately. - Repeatability recurring & revenue impact != low -> consider productization (PM ticket and estimate). - One-off low-effort & low-risk -> Sales Ops can approve with templated discount. This canvas also contains a numeric scoring formula: score = revenue_weight*revenue_bucket + risk_weight*risk_bucket + effort_penalty - repeatability_bonus (weights defined on Confluence).
triage_flow: Step 1: Intake submission by AE/CS via form -> auto-populate CRM ticket. Step 2: Automated pre-check runs (check for existing commitment contracts, billing PII flags, marketplace SKU presence). Step 3: Route based on matrix to a primary owner. Step 4: Primary owner applies template response within SLA or escalates to cross-functional review. Step 5: If product change needed, PM creates PM-xxxx ticket, links intake as customer impact example, and assigns priority per scoring. Step 6: Finance approves any invoicing/commitment deviations before customer acceptance. SLA targets: initial ack within 4 business hours, decision or next-steps within 3 business days for medium complexity, 10 business days for high complexity requiring legal/finance. Exceptions: emergency legal holds or enterprise contract negotiations may suspend SLA and require exec escalation.
example_requests: Customer requests a 12-month committed usage discount tier not in public pricing
Enterprise asks to split invoice into department-level cost-allocation tags
Marketplace partner requests reduced marketplace fee for initial pilot
Customer requests invoice net-90 instead of net-30 for high ARR deal
CS asks for temporary price override for a technical outage compensation
